fieldMarks: Mottled black and white, often arranged in bands across the back and tail
Hatchlings have similar markings and bright green heads; the green fades after about one month
behavior: Terrestrial, rarely climbs more than a few feet, strong swimmer
Retreats into burrows for winter brumation; in south Florida emerges from about February
Omnivore and efficient egg predator of ground-nesting birds and reptiles
habitat: Savannas and disturbed habitats such as forest clearings, roadsides and fence rows; tolerates flooded marshes.
range: Native to Brazil, Paraguay, Bolivia, Uruguay and Argentina. Breeding populations in Florida (Hillsborough, Miami-Dade and Charlotte counties per FWC); NatureServe lists Florida and Georgia as established and possibly South Carolina. Not native to Canada.
